judge_assessment.explanation: Every claim the judge makes survives independent checking. I re-solved all eight problems from the worksheet text: 3x+7=25 gives x=6; (2x+5)+(x+3)=26 gives x=6 and AB=17; 5(x-2)=3x+8 gives x=9; 4x-1=2x+7 gives x=4 and AM=15; 3x+(x+2)+(2x-1)=37 gives x=6 and BC=8; 3x+4=5x-12 gives x=8 and AB=28; 2(x+3)=4x-10 gives x=8; and in problem 8, 2x-3=x+5 gives x=8, AB=13 and AC=13+6=19 -- exactly the values the judge lists and exactly what verify.json holds. The synthesis proof in the key is also correct and non-circular: it adds the shared BC to both sides (Addition Property) BEFORE invoking the Segment Addition Postulate on AC and BD. What the judge did not reach is a verification-coverage gap. Problem 5(a) prints 'Name the postulate that lets you add the three short segments to get AD' as part of the question, and verify.json id 5 carries only a solve (x=6) and an eval (BC=8) -- no manual entry -- while the IDENTICAL naming prompt in problem 2(a) does carry one ('Naming the Segment Addition Postulate as the statement that licenses AB + BC = AC'). The delivered answer key shows the same asymmetry: problems 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 each end with a 'Manual review:' note and problem 5 has none. So the sheet's own convention was broken at one problem, and the delivery message inherits the slip: final_response.md reports 'Twenty checks in total' with 'Six items ... flagged for manual review', while verify.json holds 21 entries of which 7 are manual (the key's own Curriculum block prints '21 tagged checks').

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 7's planted flawed proof is a real, diagnosable error rather than an arithmetic slip: Jordan's line 3 writes '6 = 4x - 10' with the reason 'Subtraction Property of Equality', i.e. 2x is removed from the left side only. The key names line 3 as the first wrong line, states what the property actually licenses, and then disproves Jordan's x=4 numerically -- 2(7)=14 against 4(4)-10=6 -- so the student sees the check that would have caught it.

Problem 8 pairs a general two-column proof with a numeric instance of the same configuration: the model proof reaches AC = BD by adding the common BC to congruent outer segments, and part (b) then makes it concrete with AB = 13, BC = 6, AC = 19 and the closing check BD = 6 + 13 = 19.

The value-free reference diagram at the top of page 1 (A, B, C, D collinear, captioned 'No values shown -- use the lengths given in each problem') fixes the labelling convention once, so no problem's figure can be misread as another problem's data.

The key distinguishes a right statement from a right reason: on problem 3 it warns that a student writing '2x - 10 = 8' with the reason 'combined like terms' has the correct statement and the wrong justification, because the terms sit on opposite sides of the equals sign.

root_causes.description: Coverage is enforced per problem id rather than per printed response slot, so a problem that prints a naming prompt alongside its numeric parts satisfies the gate with the numeric entries alone. Problem 5(a)'s 'Name the postulate' answer is therefore the one printed request on the sheet that no verify entry and no answer-key grading note covers.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 5: '(a) Name the postulate that lets you add the three short segments to get AD, then write and solve the equation: x = ___  (b) Find the length BC.' -- three requested responses.
verify.json id 5 has exactly two entries: {'type': 'solve', 'expr': '3*x+(x+2)+(2*x-1)-37', 'expected': [6]} and {'type': 'eval', 'expr': 'x+2', 'expected': 8}. No manual entry exists for id 5.

verify.json id 2 shows the intended convention: alongside its solve and eval it carries {'type': 'manual', 'desc': 'Naming the Segment Addition Postulate as the statement that licenses AB + BC = AC ...'} for the same kind of prompt.
answer_key.pdf prints a 'Manual review' note under problems 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8; problem 5's solution ends at the check '18 + 8 + 11 = 37 cm' with no grading note for the naming half.

improvements.title: Cover problem 5's 'Name the postulate' request with a manual entry, and enforce slot-level coverage generally
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule in SKILL.md from 'every problem id carries at least one check' to 'every response the problem text requests carries a check or an explicit manual entry', and enforce it in the gate chain: extend tests/check_layout.py (or a sibling checker invoked from scripts/build.sh) to count the request cues inside each \problem body -- lettered parts (a)/(b)/(c), imperative prompts such as 'Name the', 'State the', 'Explain', 'Say which' -- and fail when the number of requested responses for an id exceeds the number of verify entries bound to it. For this case that forces a manual entry on id 5 mirroring id 2's, and the answer key would then print the matching grading note.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem body reads '(a) Name the postulate that licenses this equation. (b) Solve for x.' with a verify.json carrying only a solve entry for that id: the checker must exit non-zero naming the uncovered request. The same fixture with an added manual entry must pass. Against today's chain the fixture builds green (curr-303 did, with gate-summary layout-ws PASS), so the assertion fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the internal inconsistency where two identically phrased naming prompts on the same sheet are treated differently, and makes the manual-item count reported to the teacher accurate -- final_response.md's 'six items ... flagged for manual review' becomes the true seven.
improvements.risk: Cue-based counting will over-trigger on prose that merely narrates ('the key names the postulate'), so it must read only inside \problem bodies and needs an author-visible override for a request that is genuinely rhetorical.

case_summary: A correct and well-built short-proof workshop. All eight problems and every requested length re-solve to the values in verify.json and the key (x = 6, 6, 9, 4, 6, 8, 8, 8; AB = 17, AM = 15, BC = 8, AB = 28, AB = 13, AC = 19), the study guide's three try-its check out (x = 5, x = 6, x = 5), and the two-column tables leave real work for the student while structuring it. One defect the judge did not reach: problem 5(a) asks the student to name the Segment Addition Postulate and nothing verifies or flags that answer, even though problem 2(a) asks the same thing and is correctly flagged manual -- the same slip shows up in the answer key (no 'Manual review' note on problem 5) and in final_response.md, which reports 20 checks and 6 manual items where verify.json holds 21 and 7.
